From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP kickoff: Novum evaluation & timeline coordination

Hi Ashley —

Thanks again for the conversation last week. As discussed, I put together a short mutual action plan (attached) and a companion evaluation checklist to keep the pilot focused and on a tight timeline. High level:

- Goal: Validate Redwood inference for Novum’s document-parsing assistant (latency, cost, and quality on your sample corpus).
- Target eval window: 3–4 weeks starting next week.
- Proposed close: finalize recommended configuration and next steps by 2026-08-21 (flexible if you need an extra week).

To make the kickoff productive, please confirm:
1) Who from your engineering team will be the point for integration (API keys, network egress, sample data)?
2) Any hard constraints (on-prem proxies, restricted egress, SSO) we should know about pre-kickoff?
3) Proposed times for a 45-minute kickoff: Wed 7/21 morning (9–11 PT) or Thu 7/22 afternoon (1–3 PT) — pick two options and we’ll send a calendar invite.

Attached: Redwood_MAP_v1.pdf (draft MAP) and eval_plan_novum.xlsx (high-level tests + success criteria). Jasmine (SE) and Connor (CS) are looped for technical and success planning.

Look forward to starting.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin

Hi Ashley + Marcus — great to meet you both (virtually). I’m the Solutions Engineer who will lead the technical evaluation with Novum. A few items I’ll aim to cover in the kickoff and in the pre-kickoff checklist below so we can hit the ground running: 

Pre-kickoff technical checklist (please share if available):
- Sample dataset (or a synthetic subset) representative of token lengths and average document size.
- Expected QPS / concurrency during peak test windows.
- Typical input sequence length (avg / 95th percentile) and any long-tail cases.
- Network: egress IP allowlist, proxy details, or private connectivity requirements.
- Auth: will you want us to use short-lived keys or temporary API credentials?
- Security/compliance: any required SOC2 evidence or data handling constraints we should attach to the MAP.

During the kickoff I’ll demo a quick baseline run (simple generation latencies and embedding throughput), walk through the eval plan steps in the spreadsheet, and agree on success metrics (latency P90, token cost per inference, quality gates). If Wed 7/21 10:30 PT is confirmed I’ll prepare a short tech-readout (10–15m) and a runbook for the first two test pulses.

Marcus — looping back on the MAP rollout responsibilities so Diego knows who to contact for each item.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.com

Hi all — Diego here, engineering lead at Novum. Thanks for the intro, Ashley. Quick context from our side: 

- We’ll need to sanitize or tokenize any production PII before it leaves our environment. We can provide a representative synthetic subset that mirrors length and structure.
- Network: we run egress through a managed proxy and can provide an allowlist of outbound IPs; we prefer ephemeral API keys.
- SSO: we use Okta — if there are admin flows to request access to logs or dashboards, let’s capture that in the MAP.

I’ll upload a short infra readme (attached) with the proxy and SSO notes. For kickoff, 7/21 10:30 PT is good — I’ll join.

Cheers,
Diego Ramos
Engineering Lead | Novum AI
diego.ramos@novum.ai
